paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens, showing how a baseline model (MistralV0.2-Base) and versions fine-tuned on different medical specialties score across six sets of per-specialty terms. The category axis is horizontal and labeled “Per-specialty terms,” with six groups ordered left to right as Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The value axis is vertical and labeled “Negative log probability,” displayed on a linear scale with tick marks at approximately 1-unit intervals, ranging from about −27 at the bottom to about −22 at the top. Each x-axis group contains seven adjacent bars (grouped side-by-side, not stacked) corresponding to the legend at the top: a light-blue bar for “MistralV0.2-Base,” followed by six fine-tuned variants colored from very light peach to progressively darker orange/brown for “Cardio,” “Gastro,” “Infect,” “Neuro,” “Obstetrics,” and “Pediatrics.” In the Cardio terms group, the light-blue baseline bar reaches roughly −26.7, while the fine-tuned bars cluster around approximately −25.7 to −26.1. In the Gastro terms group, the baseline is around −24.8 and the fine-tuned bars are around roughly −23.9 to −24.3. In the Infect terms group, the baseline is about −23.7 and the fine-tuned bars lie near approximately −22.9 to −23.3. In the Neuro terms group, the baseline is about −25.4 and the fine-tuned bars are around roughly −24.2 to −24.7. In the Obstetrics terms group, the baseline is about −24.7 and the fine-tuned bars are near approximately −23.8 to −24.1. In the Pediatrics terms group, the baseline is about −24.7 and the fine-tuned bars are around roughly −23.6 to −24.0. The bar ordering within each group appears consistent with the legend (baseline first, then the six fine-tuning specialties), and no individual bars are outlined, annotated, or otherwise specially emphasized beyond the color coding.
